title: fb-ads-agent client.config.json
description: Every per-client fact for a Facebook/Meta Ads agent. A client reset touches this file only, never code. Validated by the hand-rolled validator in scripts/scaffold.mjs (2020-12 subset: type/enum/const/required/properties/additionalProperties/minLength/minItems/minimum/maximum/pattern/format:uri/$ref/allOf/if-then).

acceptance.description: Verification-first completion criteria derived from the task brief / one-shot intake. Criteria here are the durable source of truth for what must PASS (script-verifiable) or PARK (human gate) before the agent can claim done.

goalCondition.description: Paste-ready Claude Code /goal condition for this client, e.g. require verify to exit 0 and every configured creative/optimizer criterion to be PASS or PARKED with evidence.

verification.description: How this criterion is checked: command, artifact path, API preflight, or named human gate.

gate.description: Optional human gate owner/name when the criterion cannot be fully machine-checked.

verifier.description: Who decides this criterion. code = a registered check in scripts/verify-acceptance.registry.mjs keyed by this id; external = a third-party service's verdict read by a registered check; human = PARKED at the named gate, never self-graded by the agent that produced the artifact. Omitted: gate present => human, else code.

negativeCase.description: The fixture or scenario where this check correctly FAILS. A check that cannot be made to fail is not a check. Every code/external criterion needs one (test/acceptance.test.mjs proves them); verify-acceptance fail-closes on unregistered ids either way.

params.description: Thresholds and knobs the registered check reads (e.g. {"expected": 15} for a batch-size floor). Keeps the criterion self-contained: the check function decides HOW, params say HOW MUCH.

maxAttempts.description: Bound on the fix->rerun-verify goal loop. Exhausting it is a legitimate terminal FAIL: report with evidence, never round up to done.

slug.description: Folder slug; also drives creative_id and cross-client self-identity.

landing_page.description: Destination URL for every ad. NEVER a homepage guess or a placeholder; a link containing TODO or example.com is rejected at publish.

geo.description: Country codes to target. Default US-only (the reference Canada mistake). e.g. ["US"].

page_id.description: Facebook page the ads run under.

instagram_id.description: Optional IG actor id for IG placements. IG profile must have a profile photo before ads run.

access_token_env.description: NAME of the env var holding the Meta token (value never in config). Default FB_ACCESS_TOKEN.

static.description: Testing adset id for image ads.

video.description: Testing adset id for video ads.

testing.description: Testing campaign (20% budget by convention; new creative lands here PAUSED).

winners.description: Winners campaign (CBO; proven creative is duplicated here).

conversion_action_type.description: The lead/conversion action type used to count leads (e.g. offsite_conversion.custom.<id> or lead).

segments.description: OPTIONAL: multiple campaign segments (e.g. advisor + SMB), each with its own adsets, campaigns, and landing page. Absent = single-segment (the top-level adsets/campaigns/client.landing_page, unchanged). A format targets a segment via formats[].segment; unassigned formats use the top-level default segment.

statics_per_day.description: Image creatives generated per day (reference sweet spot: 10).

image_model.description: Image generation model (was hardcoded in the reference; now config). e.g. google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview or a kie nano-banana model.

utm_template.description: url_tags template for creatives (was hardcoded). e.g. utm_content={{ad.id}}&ad_id={{ad.id}}.

formats.description: Creative LAYOUT/vibe tags (the 'format' axis). Closed set per client.

rules.description: Prompt/QA rules for this layout (e.g. iMessage UI coherence, flat screen-grab only).

persona_key.description: Optional: bind this format to ONE persona (folded-tag clients whose tag already encodes who). When set, the format contributes one cell, not a Cartesian expansion.

insight_key.description: Optional: bind this format to ONE insight/pain point (folded-tag clients).

fixed_prompt.description: Optional: pin the EXACT generation prompt (snapshot-driven creative, e.g. fixed headline cards) instead of composing generatively from brand fields.

segment.description: Optional: which meta_ads.segments[].name this format publishes to (multi-segment clients). Unset = the default (top-level) segment.

personas.description: Audience axis ('persona_key'). Who the ad targets.

insights.description: Message axis ('insight_key'). The pain point / angle.

generation_rules.description: e.g. logo policy, confidential-name rule. Resolve the reference's logo contradiction per client here.

confidential_name.description: If true, never render or mention the brand name in public-facing ad copy/images.

target_cpl.description: Target cost per lead. The kill/promote pivot.

enable_ctr_rule.description: DEMOTED to a zero-conversion tiebreaker (7/14 house standard): DEAD_CREATIVE only fires when leads === 0, so a converting ad can never be killed on CTR alone. High CTR is not a keep signal either - Andromeda optimizes toward clicks that don't convert.

min_ctr.description: CTR floor for the (zero-conversion-only) DEAD_CREATIVE tiebreaker.

promote_on_first_conversion.description: Winners-lineage: promote a testing ad on its FIRST conversion (>=1 lead), regardless of CPL (the campaign-manager rule - CPL is never compared to target in testing). High-CPL winners are weeded downstream by the winners-campaign kill (kill_cpa_multiple_of_avg / stall), NOT by a testing bad_cpl kill. target_cpl still gates the zero-conversion kill (ZERO_CONV_BURN); it does NOT gate bad_cpl for a converting ad in this mode (a converter promotes before bad_cpl is reached).

kill_cpa_multiple_of_avg.description: Winners-lineage kill: sunset a WINNERS-campaign ad whose CPA exceeds this multiple of the running average CPA across winners (e.g. 2 = the 2x-average rule). Dynamic, not target-anchored.

kill_cpa_floor.description: Winners-lineage stall kill: a day counts as bad when CPA >= this floor (or spend>0 with zero conversions).

kill_stall_days.description: Winners-lineage stall kill: sunset after this many consecutive bad days.

conversion_recency_days.description: House standard (7/14 sync): KEEP any testing ad with >=1 conversion within this many trailing days (reason RECENT_CONVERTER) - recency outranks CPL; only hard_cpa_cap beats it. Default 3. Requires per-day insight rows (time_increment=1); with aggregate-only insights the rule cannot fire and legacy behavior applies.

hard_cpa_cap.description: ABSOLUTE cost-per-conversion ceiling (currency, not a multiple of target_cpl) - the runaway-spend circuit breaker. Kills regardless of recent conversions, _WINNER tag, or promote_on_first_conversion. With zero leads it breaches once spend alone passes the cap. null (default) disables. Set the client's real number at stamp time; $100 was an example on the 7/14 call, not a default.

kill_action.description: What a kill decision emits. PAUSE (default) stops spend but paused ads STILL COUNT toward Meta's ad-per-ad-set cap; DELETE frees the slot (Meta auto-archives; historical reporting kept) and is required to unblock a capped testing ad set. DELETE is the bigger external write - it stays behind DRY_RUN + explicit approval like every Meta write.

dashboard.description: Optional dashboard branding. pipeline.mjs embeds these tokens into dashboard/data.json; the static dashboard/index.html applies them as CSS variables. Colors default to the fleet-neutral clean white/black monochrome (#1a1a1a / #4a4a4a on white) when omitted.

title.description: Dashboard page title. Defaults to '<client.name> - Meta Ads'.

initials.description: Logo-badge initials. Defaults to the first letters of client.name.

primary.description: Primary brand color (hex): headings, logo badge, stat values.

vision_qa.description: Vision QA grading knobs (vision-qa.mjs). Optional; omit for defaults.

model.description: Anthropic vision model that grades creatives against config.brand. Default claude-opus-4-8. The grader is intentionally a DIFFERENT model call than generation: an independent verdict, never self-graded.
